paragraphs: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov held a brief 20-minute meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.
This marked the first direct diplomatic encounter between top German and Russian officials since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The meeting took place despite escalating tensions, following German accusations that Russia orchestrated a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport. During the talks, Wadephul urged Moscow to abandon its dangerous path of escalation toward Germany, Europe, and NATO. While Lavrov downplayed the event’s importance and claimed Germany made no position changes, diplomats noted the symbolic weight of reopening a direct channel. Both sides disputed who initiated the exchange.

Despite Germany’s primary role as a strategic supporter of Ukraine rather than a mediator, the meeting reflects broader shifts in diplomatic discussions as international leaders search for ways toward future negotiations.

paragraphs: German Foreign Minister met Russian Foreign Minister at the UN in New York. This was their first meeting since Russia invaded Ukraine over four years ago.

The talks lasted only 20 minutes and happened during a time of high tension between both countries. Germany recently accused Russia of planning a drone attack at a German airport. The German minister told Russia to stop its dangerous actions against Europe and NATO. Russia said the meeting changed nothing, and both countries disagreed on who asked for the talk.

Germany still strongly supports Ukraine with weapons and help. But this short meeting shows that leaders are starting to talk directly again as world organizations try to find peaceful solutions to end the war.
